questions.text:
Consider three floating point numbers A, B and C stored in registers [latex]R_A[/latex], [latex]R_B[/latex] and [latex]R_C[/latex], respectively as per IEEE-754 single precision floating point format. The 32-bit content stored in these registers (in hexadecimal form) are as follows.

[latex]R_A=0xC1400000[/latex]
[latex]R_B=0x42100000[/latex]
[latex]R_C=0x41400000[/latex]

Which one of the following is FALSE?
questions.solution:
Decode each number (sign | exponent | mantissa):
- [latex]R_A=[/latex] C1400000: sign 1, exponent [latex]130\Rightarrow2^3[/latex], mantissa 1.1[latex]{}_2[/latex] = 1.5 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]A=-12[/latex]
- [latex]R_B=[/latex] 42100000: sign 0, exponent [latex]132\Rightarrow2^5[/latex], mantissa 1.001[latex]{}_2[/latex] = 1.125 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]B=36[/latex]
- [latex]R_C=[/latex] 41400000: same as A but positive [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]C=12[/latex]

- [latex]A+C=0[/latex] True
- [latex]A+B=24\ne12=C[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] FALSE
- [latex]B=36=3C[/latex] True
- [latex]B-C=24 \gt 0[/latex] True

Answer: C = A + B

questions.text: Consider four processes P, Q, R, and S scheduled on a CPU as per round robin algorithm with a time quantum of 4 units. The processes arrive in the order P, Q, R, S, all at time t = 0. There is exactly one context switch from S to Q, exactly one context switch from R to Q, and exactly two context switches from Q to R. There is no context switch from S to P. Switching to a ready process after the termination of another process is also considered a context switch. Which one of the following is NOT possible as CPU burst time (in time units) of these processes?
questions.solution:
Simulate round robin (quantum 4, order P, Q, R, S) for option 4: P = 3, Q = 7, R = 7, S = 3.
- P runs 3 and finishes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q runs 4 (3 left) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R runs 4 (3 left) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] S runs 3 and finishes
- [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q runs 3 and finishes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R runs 3 and finishes

Switches: P[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]Q, Q[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]R, R[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]S, S[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]Q, Q[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]R. There is no R [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q switch, but exactly one is required. So these burst times are impossible.

(Simulating the other three options gives exactly one S[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]Q, one R[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]Q, two Q[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]R and no S[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]P.)

Answer: P = 3, Q = 7, R = 7, S = 3

j stays 0, and the loops print [latex]a[i][0][k][/latex] for k = 0, 1, 2:

'P' = 80 = 0101 0000, 'x' = 120 = 0111 1000.

- [latex]a\,\&\,b[/latex] = 0101 0000 = 80; 80 + '*'(42) = 122 = 'z'
- [latex]a\,|\,b[/latex] = 0111 1000 = 120; 120 [latex]-[/latex] '-'(45) = 75 = 'K'
- [latex]a\oplus b[/latex] = 0010 1000 = 40; 40 + '+'(43) = 83 = 'S'

printf uses %c, so it prints characters: z K S

Answer: z K S

Using Doolittle LU (unit diagonal in L):
- Row 1 of U = [1, 1, [latex]-[/latex]2]; [latex]L_{21}=1,\ L_{31}=2[/latex]
- [latex]U_{22}=3-1=2,\ U_{23}=-1-(-2)=1[/latex]
- [latex]L_{32}=\frac{1-2\cdot1}{2}=-\frac12[/latex]
- [latex]U_{33}=-5-2(-2)-(-\frac12)(1)=-\frac12[/latex]

Solving the system: eq2 [latex]-[/latex] eq1 gives [latex]2x_2+x_3=3[/latex]; eq3 [latex]-[/latex] 2[latex]\cdot[/latex]eq1 gives [latex]x_2+x_3=1[/latex]. So [latex]x_2=2,\ x_3=-1,\ x_1=4-2-2=0[/latex].

Answer: [latex]L_{32}=-\frac12,\ U_{33}=-\frac12,\ x_1=0[/latex]
